scope: Unsubscribed (zero-cost) path: scripts/benchmark_hooks.py --provider claude --shell direct --samples 20 --idle-seconds 3, alternating the adapter built from the parent commit (base, 9ea22f7) with the WD-140 adapter (new), same host, same session. The benchmark event is Stop, which is never subscribed, so it measures the one extra bounded read of policy/socket.json and nothing else.

wd027_reference.note: Not reproducible on the host as measured today: the unmodified parent-commit adapter measures 35.6 ms sequential p50 here, so absolute WD-027 numbers cannot be used as a regression bar on this host.

same_directory_runs.note: Re-run after review because the first_ms gap in the table above looked consistent. Both executables copied into one directory (base-hook.exe, new-hook.exe), alternating, 4 rounds. Round 1 was disturbed for both (host CPU 22-27 %).

reading: Warm path: sequential p50 is 34-38 ms for both adapters in the undisturbed rounds (base 34.0-37.7, new 36.3-37.7), sequential p95 is 39-46 ms for both, and concurrent-four p95 overlaps (base 82-139 ms, new 85-100 ms); no difference is distinguishable from host noise. First call (the cold process): the new adapter is consistently about 5-8 ms slower in undisturbed rounds (new 48.2-56.8 ms against base 42.8-48.4 ms, both with the binaries in one directory and in two), so the one extra discovery-file read plus the larger binary shows up on a cold start. That is a small measured cost, not a null result; WD-154 re-measures it on a quiet host. The host cannot reproduce the WD-027 absolute numbers (29.4 ms sequential p50).
